Aiyo, you want to hear how I'm managing my little patch this year? Let me think it through. I'm 73, been farming this same soil for 50 years. My wife passed some time back, the children work in town, so it's just me now. Three mu isn't much, but it keeps me busy and puts some grain in the bin.

**My fields this year**

I split the three mu the way I always do — two mu in wheat followed by maize, one mu in cotton on the western patch. That's how I've done it for years. The cotton patch has sandier soil, it never did well for wheat anyway. Some of my neighbors dropped cotton because the picking is too much work, and honestly at my age I feel it too. My back doesn't bend like it used to. But I kept one mu because cotton still brings better cash than grain, and I hire a niece and a neighbor woman to help me pick in the fall — I pay them by the jin.

**Wheat (already in the ground, 2 mu)**

I planted in mid-October last fall, the same Jimai variety I've been using — I saved some seed and bought a bit fresh, around 15 jin per mu. Before planting I spread about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 kind, roughly 25 kg per mu. That's my base. Now around jointing in early April I already topdressed some urea, about 15 kg per mu, when I gave it the first spring irrigation. Wheat needs water at jointing and at filling — two irrigations from the well is my usual. If it rains good in May I might skip the filling one, pumping costs money and the meter adds up. I sprayed once for weeds in March, the village shop sells a cheap herbicide mix that does the job. Harvest will be around June 10-15, I pay the combine man 60 yuan per mu, he comes through the village.

**Maize (coming after wheat, 2 mu)**

The moment the combine leaves I have to plant maize, no time to till properly — I just do no-till, the custom planter comes and drops the seed right into the stubble. I use Zhengdan or whatever hybrid the shop pushes that year, about 2 kg seed per mu, costs around 50 yuan. I put down about 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting and then topdress urea around 15 kg per mu at the big-trumpet stage in late July. If it rains enough in July-August I won't irrigate — this maize usually takes care of itself if heaven gives water. If it's dry I'll run the well once. I spray once for corn borer, maybe twice if I see bad ones. Harvest end of September.

**Cotton (1 mu, planting right now)**

I'm laying the mulch film this week, planting should be done by April 25. I bought Bt cotton seed from the town shop, the kind that resists bollworm — without it I couldn't manage, the spraying would kill me. About 2 kg seed per mu. I put down a bag of compound fertilizer before laying film, around 25 kg per mu, and I'll topdress urea around 10 kg when the bolls start forming. Cotton needs watching — I spray maybe 3-4 times through the summer for aphids and spider mites, that's the real cost. I'll irrigate once at flowering if it's dry. Picking starts September, I pay helpers to come pick — I can't bend all day anymore.

**What worries me**

Pumping costs keep creeping up. Last year my electricity for the well was higher than I remembered. If prices go up again I'll cut one irrigation on the maize. And my body — I already told my nephew if something happens I may have to rent out a mu or two. But this year I can still manage.
